passages.t: ‘When I am afraid, I put my trust in You’, and tears in God's bottle
passages.happening:
The heading sets the scene: “A Miktam of David, when the Philistines seized him in Gath” (verse 1). It also names a tune, “A Dove on Distant Oaks” (verse 1).

David is surrounded. “Be merciful to me, O God, for men are hounding me; all day they press their attack” (verse 1). They twist his words and watch his steps (verses 5 and 6).

In the middle of that, one of the simplest prayers in the Bible. “When I am afraid, I put my trust in You” (verse 3). And then: “in God I trust. I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?” (verse 4). The same words come back as a refrain in verses 10 and 11.

Verse 8 is tender. “You have taken account of my wanderings. Put my tears in Your bottle” (verse 8). The psalm ends with thanks: “For You have delivered my soul from death, and my feet from stumbling, that I may walk before God in the light of life” (verse 13).
passages.hearers:
Gath was one of the five chief cities of the Philistines, Israel's enemies. David fled there from Saul. When he was recognised, he “was very much afraid of Achish the king of Gath” (1 Samuel 21:12), and escaped by pretending to be mad. Psalm 34 is also linked to that day. Samuel does not say he was ‘seized’, so some read the heading as a summary of his danger. The book page explains the headings, and ‘Miktam’, a word whose meaning is not known.

The ‘bottle’ is a skin bottle, the goatskin bag for carrying water or wine. A tear kept in it is a tear treasured, not spilled and lost. God's ‘book’ was a picture of a king's records. The God who keeps account of wrongs also keeps account of his servant's sorrow.

The vows of verse 12 were promises made in danger, to bring a thank offering when God rescued.
passages.later:
The letter to the Hebrews quotes Psalm 118:6, which has almost the same words as this psalm's refrain: “The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?” (Hebrews 13:6).

Jesus said that not one sparrow is forgotten by God, and “even the very hairs of your head are all numbered” (Luke 12:7). At the end of the Bible, “God will wipe away every tear from their eyes” (Revelation 7:17).
passages.asks:
Verse 3 does not say ‘I am never afraid.’ It says, ‘When I am afraid.’ Fear comes. Trust is what you do with it.

Verse 8 is for anyone who has cried where no one saw. God saw. Not one tear was wasted or forgotten. You can tell him about each one.
